newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge narrows case vs. lobbyist in Espy probe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge narrows case vs. lobbyist in Espy probe.

text.p: A federal judge has dismissed two of 19 criminal counts against a lobbyist indicted on charges he gave illegal gifts to then-Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy, court papers showed on Friday.

U.S. District Court Judge Thelton Henderson in San Francisco granted a pretrial defense motion to dismiss two counts against lobbyist Richard Douglas, a longtime friend of Espy. The counts alleged that Douglas made false statements to the FBI, which was investigating Espy.
Douglas worked for Sun-Diamond Growers of California, the nation's largest fruit cooperative, at the time of the alleged offenses in 1993 and 1994 while Espy served in the cabinet.
Espy resigned in 1994 amid accusations he accepted illegal gifts and favors from companies he was supposed to regulate. He has repeatedly denied doing anything wrong.

In October 1996, a federal grand jury indicted Douglas on charges he gave illegal gifts to Espy and masterminded illegal political donations to Espy's brother. The 19-count indictment also accused Douglas of making "false statements" to federal investigators and of wire fraud in obtaining a mortgage.

In December, Douglas filed several pretrial motions, asking the court to dismiss the bulk of the charges against him. The defense argued that independent counsel Donald Smaltz lacked the jurisdiction to bring many of the charges.
The defense also asked the court to order broader discovery.
In his ruling, Henderson granted one motion to dismiss, throwing out two counts alleging Douglas made false statements to the FBI when he was questioned in June, 1994.

During that interview, Douglas denied that Sun-Diamond illegally paid expenses for Espy. He also denied that the cooperative had matters pending before the Agriculture Department while Espy was secretary.
Henderson denied six defense motions, including those to dismiss the campaign contribution and mortgage counts against Douglas, as well as motions for additional discovery.
In his ruling, Henderson said the independent counsel had the jurisdiction to bring the charges. He said the court would hold a status conference on April 14 to set a trial date.
